definitions.explanation: The act of abandoning or discarding something or someone, especially in a legal context.

examples.japanese: {死体|したい}{遺棄|いき}の{容疑|ようぎ}で{逮捕|たいほ}された。
examples.english: He was arrested on suspicion of abandoning a body.

examples.japanese: {不法|ふほう}{投棄|とうき}と{遺棄|いき}は{犯罪|はんざい}だ。
examples.english: Illegal dumping and abandonment are crimes.

examples.japanese: {化学兵器|かがくへいき}の{遺棄|いき}が{国際的|こくさいてき}な{問題|もんだい}になっている。
examples.english: The abandonment of chemical weapons has become an international issue.

notes:
A formal, legal term for abandonment. Also functions as a suru verb ({遺棄|いき}する). Most commonly encountered in news and legal contexts.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {死体|したい}{遺棄|いき} — abandonment of a body (a criminal charge)
- {遺棄|いき}{罪|ざい} — crime of abandonment
- {遺棄|いき}する — to abandon, to desert
- {化学兵器|かがくへいき}の{遺棄|いき} — abandonment of chemical weapons
- {保護|ほご}{責任者|せきにんしゃ}{遺棄|いき} — abandonment by a person with duty of care

LEGAL CONTEXT:
{遺棄|いき}{罪|ざい} is a crime under Japanese law that includes abandoning a person who needs care, or abandoning a dead body. {死体|したい}{遺棄|いき} (abandonment of a corpse) is one of the most commonly reported charges in crime news.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {放棄|ほうき} — abandonment, renunciation (broader, includes rights and claims)
- {投棄|とうき} — dumping, disposal (of waste or objects)
- {廃棄|はいき} — disposal, scrapping (of documents, equipment)
